scenes.title: Getting closer is the point.
scenes.body: A limit describes what the output approaches as the input gets closer to a value. For f(x) = x², inputs near 2 give outputs near 4.
scenes.citation: Original calculus example notes · 1.3 Limits and continuity

scenes.title: Two sides. One destination.
scenes.body: A finite two-sided limit exists when the left-hand and right-hand limits exist and agree. For x² near 2, both sides approach 4.

cards.label: Different values
cards.text: The two-sided limit does not exist.

scenes.citation: Original calculus example notes · 1.3 Limits and continuity

scenes.title: The limit can survive a hole.
scenes.body: This expression equals x + 2 when x ≠ 2. It is undefined at 2, yet its limit as x approaches 2 is still 4.
scenes.citation: Original calculus example notes · 1.3 Limits and continuity
